hypothesis: An ordinary small neural network seeing only raw selected fifth-action key, its actually observed factual effect, and raw candidate return key can learn an intervention-dependent decision when trained on properly scaled, paired factual returns; identical architecture/sampling using the historical weak R34-style target/ranking and a strong-label fifth-erased control distinguish supervision failure from information absence.

data.generator: R33 unchanged synthetic factual quartic-law FIT
data.paired_definition: Two independent selected factual return action episodes, same public world/action history, same measured selected fifth effect, opposite selected return actions; not evaluator unseen action
data.input_scope: Only raw P80 16D selected fifth action key, raw 16D selected fifth factual effect (step4), raw 16D candidate return action key; exactly 48D; NO derived context, informed-indicator, q, quartic polynomial or evaluator hindsight features
data.score_source: R33 score world generator and evaluator only
data.ood_longer_B: Bypassed in minimal positive control; not a cold-memory experiment

arms.architecture: 48D raw P80 -> Linear(48,64) -> GELU -> Linear(64,64) -> GELU -> Linear(64,1) factual cost; same architecture for all arms
arms.erased_control: Same strong loss but selected fifth factual effect all zeros in both FIT training and evaluation; selected fifth action remains, q unseen

optimization.optimizer: AdamW lr0.002 all arms weight_decay0.01 gradient_clip_norm1
optimization.weak_objective: MSE pred vs unchanged 0.1*factual selected squared goal error plus 0.1*softplus(-sign(factual_cost1-factual_cost0)*(pred1-pred0))
optimization.strong_objective: MSE pred vs 10*original factual scaled cost = actual squared goal error plus 2.0*softplus(-sign(factual_cost1-factual_cost0)*(pred1-pred0))
